sources.titleEn: Bright Seeker Cookie skill haste research
sources.summaryEn: Modelled expected Bright Seeker damage (raid only) for 43 s fights, where the team dies with 17 s left, and 30 s fights, where it dies at the 30 s slam. The model uses three gear baselines, trades rune haste against rune skill amp 1:1, and finds a haste threshold at about 40 total. Crit rate and crit damage runes never beat haste or amp. Recommendations: whales run 8 haste lines, mid spenders target total skill haste 41–45, and F2P players who die at the 30 s slam should go skill amp and crit damage, because haste is negative in 30 s fights. The author's deck (Macaron and Cheesecake on 스증, everyone levelled down to Cheesecake's ATK, Jungle Warrior instead of Herb) scored 339G 975M at 912.73M (about 372x). After Seeker went to 8★ it scored 367G 994M. Last season's max was 250x, and a low-spec variant uses 딸크 and 방어구 수리특약.

sources.summaryEn: Long beginner guide by 백산. For PvP: Arena is per server and Rumble Arena is cross-server; current Arena/Rumble gear values evasion, crit chance, crit resist, Skill Haste and Skill AMP, built as either an evasion preset or a crit-resist preset (each also with Skill AMP, crit chance, accuracy). Arena refills one ticket every 2 hours; Rumble tickets refill to max at midnight; both have a free opponent refresh every 30 minutes. Rumble's passive changes every season, so its meta changes each season. Its dungeon screenshots show a '쟁탈전' tab in the dungeon menu.

sources.title: Crumble Dungeon - Cookie Run Wiki
sources.titleEn: Cookie Run Wiki: Crumble Dungeon
sources.summaryEn: Community wiki (global). Crumble Dungeon is a Challenge Dungeon where all obtained Cookies battle the Holy Golden Drop; entry up to 3 times daily with Crumble Dungeon Keys; the squad has up to a minute to deal damage for score. The boss squashes the floor to knock Cookies back, strikes them with lightning, and summons Golden Soldier Drops. Milestone rewards run from 400,000 to 1,000,000,000,000 points; the weekly and daily ranking tables match the in-game screens in dc:67615.

sources.title: CookieRun: Crumble hub (EOG)
sources.titleEn: EOG hub: Crumble Dungeon sections (global guild)
sources.summaryEn: Global guild EOG. The Dungeon throws the whole collection at the Holy Golden Drop, scores total damage, and deploys the top 40 by combat power first; lower the levels of unwanted cookies below the 40th-place cutoff (no need for Lv.1). Controlled test on one account, 2026-08-13: 403,708,109 with a 10-star Oven Wanderer and Cool Mint deployed, 574,531,356 with both benched (+42%); a younger account showed no change. Heals and shields go to the lowest-HP ally, so divers soak the sustain; supports follow divers forward, out of the ranged dealers' range. Pomegranate's beam is read as choosing by synergy match first, which EOG flags as unconfirmed. Its simulator section: no controls; attack range sets a cookie's slot and move speed its arrival; an arena-wide shockwave throws the team back four times; the boss raises its own damage reduction three times (EOG's reading of game data: stacks to five, one application per source), so a run is decided in its first thirteen seconds; damage spent on adds scores nothing. Pets' passive effects and Collection bonuses apply to every cookie.

sources.titleEn: ND러너: Holy Golden Drop dungeon 50G+ tips
sources.summaryEn: ND러너, before the 9/10 update. Run the dungeon at least once daily: participation crystals, daily top 10 pays pet tickets and research stones, bracket and weekly rewards pay XP and coins, score milestones pay crystals. The first 40 by power deploy together. Chargers such as Oven Wanderer pull aggro and move around the boss, and summoners spread the formation, so the range-limited buffs miss; the team should stay packed in the centre. Milk captain with Passion Pay; Milk must be top ATK counting the captain's +10%; Rapid Promotion second, also for Milk. Projectile Speed synergy recipients must be Lv.1 because they take the beam first (Milk excepted). Cheesecake is also Lv.1: its ATK buff replaced Milk's stacked ATK buff, which then restarted. Two options for the beam: Macaron and Figure at ATK #1-2 with dealers levelled below them, or let Milk and the main dealers take it.

researchRecords.question: There is a small, documented set of Guild Conquest teams that KR/Global top players use to reach ≥1T damage. For each one, the community sources name the cookie lineup, levels (including deliberate Lv.1 fillers), sugar runes, gear stats, pets and perks precisely enough that someone with every cookie could reproduce it.
researchRecords.lede: What Korean and global players run in Guild Conquest (길드 토벌전), from DCInside, the official Naver cafe and crumb.gg. Every claim links its post.
researchRecords.caveat: Season 7, same Piñata. Chardonnay deck: ≥4T 647G in battle, best final 4T 300G at 4.29G. Season 7 top-10 teams unpublished; live #1 at 10T 266G.

researchRecords.question: For each PvP mode (regular Arena and Rumble Arena) there is a small documented set of top teams, and for each one the community sources name the lineup, formation, levels, stars, runes, gear, pets and the teams that beat it precisely enough that someone with every cookie could reproduce it and pick a counter.
researchRecords.seasonLabel: Arena Season 5 (live) · Rumble Arena Season 1 ends 2026-10-08; Season 2 to 2026-10-21
researchRecords.lede: What Korean and global players run in regular Arena (아레나) and Rumble Arena (와글와글 아레나). Every claim links to its post.
researchRecords.caveat: Snapshot of 2026-10-07, the eve of the 10-08 update (Lv.120 cap, Chardonnay, Rumble Season 2). Re-check after it.

researchRecords.question: For stage pushing (main stages and the Dimensional Rift past 328-30) there is a small documented set of teams, levels, runes, gear and pets that players use to clear the hardest stages at the lowest power, stated precisely enough to reproduce, including how play differs by stage type and what the recommended-power gate does to damage, in particular at the 35% and 15% damage brackets.
researchRecords.seasonLabel: Game 1.4.002 (after the 2026-09-23 stage easing) · Dimensional Rift season 1 (to 2026-10-08) · update 1.5.002 (level cap 120, stages to 364-30, Rift season 2) lands 2026-10-08
researchRecords.lede: What Korean players push main stages and the Dimensional Rift with while under-powered: the brackets, the 35% and 15% teams, and the per-boss swaps.
researchRecords.caveat: The 10-08 update (level cap 120, Rift ×1.45) moves every line. 15% screenshots: Rift bosses but GingerCraven to level 18; on stages, 289-30 Cool Mint.

researchRecords.question: The Golden Drop encounter is Crumble Dungeon, a scored mode with documented rules, and players post scores with the lineup, levels, runes, gear and perks behind them precisely enough that the top-scoring builds can be named and reproduced by someone with every cookie.
researchRecords.seasonLabel: Game 1.4.002, up to the 2026-10-08 update · Crumble Dungeon weekly boards close Thursday 00:00 KST
researchRecords.lede: Crumble Dungeon (크럼블 던전), the daily score attack on the Holy Golden Drop (황금갓방울): the rules, the top scores and the lineup rules behind them.
researchRecords.caveat: Snapshot of 2026-10-07; no Crumble Dungeon change since 9/23. Scores are players' own screenshots, one server at a time; ranked by score.

researchRecords.question: The community sources name every system that adds displayed team power in Cookie Run: Crumble, and give a cost and a power gain precise enough to rank the systems by power per unit of cost for a free and a paying player, and to say which moves a 2.2G team across the next stage-bracket line soonest.
researchRecords.seasonLabel: Game 1.4.002 with the 10-02 oven hotfix; 1.5.002 lands 2026-10-08 (cookie cap 120, Gnome Lab 130-2)
researchRecords.lede: Team power (전투력) gates stages and the Dimensional Rift: what raises it, what each source costs free and paid, posted gains, and the spend order.
researchRecords.caveat: Refreshed 2026-10-07, the day before the cap-120 update: level-120 gains are inferred or claimed, not posted. Few posted gains, all DCInside.

researchRecords.question: Players post daily dungeon clears with the lineup, pets, perks and run method precisely enough that, for each daily dungeon, the deck that clears the furthest stage on full auto can be named and reproduced, alongside the boss, entry and stage-cap facts that bound it.
researchRecords.seasonLabel: Game before the 2026-10-08 update · stage cap 770
researchRecords.lede: The daily dungeons (일일던전): each dungeon's boss and entry, and the decks that clear it furthest, full auto first.
researchRecords.caveat: Snapshot of 2026-10-07, the day before the 10-08 easing. Stages are posted screenshots and videos; ranked by stage, never by a ratio.

recordModes.lede: Regular, per-server Arena. Built Bari–Oven–Cherry Cola leads; the Rye deck is the value pick and the most-run lineup.
recordModes.caveat: crumb.gg's meta page is the only ladder data; its sample is unstated. Many 'Arena' screenshots are Rumble.

recordModes.lede: Rumble Arena (와글와글 아레나, 와레나): the cross-server arena. The top 100 still run one 12-cookie Oven–Bari team.
recordModes.caveat: Season 1's last day. Above 2,000 points levels and some defenders are hidden, so usage counts are lower bounds.

recordModes.lede: Main stages (328 chapters of 30 stages, cycling through eight zones) and the Dimensional Rift (seasonal, boss-only, opened 2026-09-23 for players past 328-30).
recordModes.caveat: Pre-easing clears (before 2026-09-23) were made against higher recommended power for 169-1 to 328-30; stage-clears.json marks the era of each.

recordModes.lede: Crumble Dungeon (크럼블 던전): every owned cookie fights the Holy Golden Drop in a timed run scored on damage, ranked daily and weekly per server.
recordModes.caveat: Fight length and boss patterns are the wiki's; damage-reduction steps are EOG's model. Entries a day: three base, lobbies show 5, a Gnome Lab node adds one.

recordModes.lede: Team power growth: every system that raises displayed team power, with its cost, cap, posted gains and the spending order by account stage.
recordModes.caveat: Power is a gate for stages and the Rift, not a measure of strength: attack types and missing stats count more.

recordModes.lede: Each daily dungeon's furthest full-auto deck, then every posted deck by stage.
recordModes.caveat: Bosses, keys and caps from patch notes and screenshots; key refunds on a loss are unconfirmed.

deckNotes.text: Tiger Lily → Herb if the team dies at the 30 s slam: 5 beams, so Tea Knight drops to Lv.1.
Cherry → Melon Soda if you're willing to tune move speed to 0.01 precision (see the Melon Soda deck).
Pet: Candy Shade Pouch once carries outlive the 17 s wipe; Panda Dumpling while the team dies there (HP 5–9M).
Cherry → Popcorn (Lv.60, no move speed), fillers Lv.50: 1T 150G at 1.86G, one poster's best; single source.
Scorpion → Herb Lv.1, Cherry and Tiger Lily kept: 9 of 10 runs line up at ~500×, lower ceiling; 1T 459G at 2.5G.
Five cookies at Lv.1, including the damage-dealer Scorpion in some versions and the buffer Pomegranate in the #1 run.
An R-rarity Cherry Cookie in an endgame team, purely for formation.
Scorpion levelled to a precise ATK window as a beam catcher rather than as a dealer.
Melon Soda → Strawberry Crepe Lv.50, or Popcorn: 1T 275G at 1.7G with both; posters split on the best of the three.
Fillers Lv.40–90, still under the 6th recipient's ATK: all twelve alive at 5.8 s left in one run.
Tiger Lily → a dealer: 1.09T at 2.32G; 저장용 tried dealers and came back to Tiger Lily.
Chardonnay under 9★: one paired test had 8★ at 3.6T vs a 9★ Macaron Cherry deck at 3.8T; 5★ "tripling" Macaron is unpaired, likely Lv.118 vs Lv.100.
Chardonnay takes a beam at any ATK, so she sits at max level without breaking the ATK order.
Cherry and move speed gone after a month as the deck's backbone.
Pet: Candy Shade Pouch. The ≈1T run (1.6G, dc:74759) swapped only the pet ('그대로 신규펫만'); its lift resistance improved alignment at the old speeds.
Pet: Panda Dumpling, if your speeds were tuned with it; a new pet's lift resistance moves placement. 867G at 1.57G (dc:76144).
Lazy variant: Tiger Lily in Herb's slot, speed only on Pinot and Melon Soda. Aligns well but breaks the multi-hit chain: lower damage.
Move speed tuned to hundredths on sugar runes to script where each cookie stops.
A 5★ Brightseeker reached 637.8G at 1.14G power, higher per power than most 10★ Cherry decks at the time.
Back to Tiger Lily once the team survives to 17 s: its average is higher, and the ceiling is similar.
Candy Shade Pouch once carries outlive the wipe; Panda Dumpling placed better while they didn't.
Fillers levelled back up after the Lv.1 era, each held just under the beam line, to survive the 17 s wipe.
Zero move speed in a Melon Soda deck: alignment left to retries.
Fillers at Lv.30, not Lv.1.
Two chargers: Cherry Cola → Rockstar or Crepe (dc:80630).
Bari 7★: Hound → Strawberry Crepe (nv:48978).
Budget: Bari 2★ at 7.45M wins up to about 9M (nv:48978).
King Choco Drop → Icy Birdie.
Evasion version with Vampire and Peach (dc:74043).
A server #1 ran Ion and Hound at Lv.1 and Herb at Lv.70 (dc:77213).
Zero Skill Haste on gear.
Grapevine → Rockstar: see arena-rye-rockstar.
Skating Queen + Grapevine → Brightseeker + Doughnut King only with 5★+ Brightseeker (arena-rye-seeker).
Grapevine → Doughnut King: 4.2% of crumb.gg's Arena sample.
Chargemellow → Icy Birdie or King Choco Drop.
One damage dealer in a 12-cookie team.
Skating Queen in a PvP deck (disputed).
Doughnut King → Skating Queen; Herb → Angel (replies on dc:81275).
Espresso was the old flex; Rockstar replaced it (dc:77725).
A 10.17M version adds Grapevine and Crepe (dc:79151).
SR Rockstar in a top Rye deck.
Ion → Strawberry Crepe (dc:76602).
Add Rockstar: the dc:78543 version.
Two ranged carries against the one-carry consensus.
Chargemellow → Hot Doggie (dc:69591).
Bari version with Vampire, Bari, Cherry Cola and Peach (dc:74043).
Evasion gear instead of crit RES and DR.
Lime in a top-10 team.
Schwarzwälder, Dr. Bones and Twizzly Gummy in a top defense.
Crepe on ATK% + move speed + Skill Haste for a turn-one front-line nuke.
Herb → Espresso (dc:70980). crumb.gg's version runs Crepe for Herb.
Herb → Rockstar: 6.1% of crumb.gg's sample, rising; #3 on 10-07 shows it.

gearRecs.substats: Skill amp + crit dmg
gearRecs.why: Crit dmg over crit rate: the crit buffer pushes crit rate far past 100% (Brightseeker 710% with an 8★ Chardonnay). Target at +15: skill amp 9%+, crit dmg 20%+. Skill amp beats displayed power.

gearRecs.substats: Skill amp + crit rate, or skill amp + flat ATK (Season 7)
gearRecs.why: Disputed after Chardonnay: 서신우 runs crit rate; one poster scored 2.6T on flat ATK vs 2.2T on crit dmg.

gearRecs.substats: Skill amp + crit rate (arena)
gearRecs.why: In arena, enemy crit resistance eats crit rate, so crit rate is the arena pick. Several raid players run the arena set and lose damage.

gearRecs.substats: Skill haste + skill amp
gearRecs.why: The only slot group that rolls both of the raid's key stats. Max haste roll is +4.6 at plate +15.

gearRecs.substats: Damage reduction + HP
gearRecs.why: Crit resistance does nothing against the raid boss. Survive the 30 s slam and reach the 17 s wipe.

gearRecs.substats: Skill haste + damage reduction
gearRecs.why: Skill amp can't roll here. This group is the only one with both haste and damage reduction.

gearRecs.substats: 6 skill-haste lines + 6 skill-amp lines, then crit, then spare damage reduction
gearRecs.why: Each piece has a fixed option pool, so 6 of each is the ceiling across 12 pieces.

gearRecs.substats: No move speed, accuracy or focus
gearRecs.why: Move speed breaks the Cherry formation. The boss has low evasion and resistance, so accuracy and focus (stage stats) are dead lines.

gearRecs.substats: Skill amp and crit dmg accessories
gearRecs.why: Plate these to +20 first: second-hand on the Season 6 #1, who has +20s and +25s. A +20 weapon ≈ a +15 accessory. Unverified.

gearRecs.substats: Separate raid preset (since 9/23)
gearRecs.why: Gear presets let raid gear stop doubling as arena gear. Posters describe the switch as a big jump.

gearRecs.substats: Skill AMP + crit rate
gearRecs.why: Crit rate beats crit DMG: opponents stack crit RES and Moon Rabbit cuts crit. One accuracy line optional.

gearRecs.substats: Skill Haste + Skill AMP (Rye and Brightseeker decks)
gearRecs.why: The only Skill Haste a Rye deck keeps: three lines.

gearRecs.substats: Skill AMP + crit rate (Bari decks)
gearRecs.why: Zero haste: Bari decks stake the fight on the first hit.

gearRecs.substats: Crit RES + DR
gearRecs.why: Most Arena damage crits. Past about 60% crit RES, DR is worth more.

gearRecs.substats: Skill Haste + crit RES (or DR)
gearRecs.why: Kept the sixth Skill Haste line while adding survival.
gearRecs.obsoleteReason: Swapping this haste for DR + crit RES won far more often; posters call six haste a scam.

gearRecs.substats: DR + crit RES (or DR + HP)
gearRecs.why: Replaced Skill Haste here: the team survives the opening far more often.

gearRecs.substats: Skill Haste on all six right-side pieces
gearRecs.why: Whoever cast first won, so heal and shield decks ran six haste lines.

gearRecs.substats: Skill Haste lines: Bari decks 0, Rye and Brightseeker decks 3
gearRecs.why: Bari decks bet on the first hit; Rye decks trade haste for survival.

gearRecs.substats: About 230% unbuffed crit on a Bari deck
gearRecs.why: So the dive still crits through Moon Rabbit's debuff.

gearRecs.substats: No accuracy or focus (at most one accuracy line)
gearRecs.why: Typical evasion is about 650, so accuracy is dead weight outside evasion matchups.

gearRecs.substats: A separate arena preset
gearRecs.why: PvP lines show little power, so the preset looks weaker than it is.

gearRecs.substats: Top rankers attack on their stage (accuracy) preset

gearRecs.substats: Highest displayed power first
gearRecs.why: The bracket follows displayed power: roll for power ('순수 뻥투'), weapons and plates first; crit resist and crit dmg inflate most. Near-ties: Skill AMP, Haste or DR.

gearRecs.substats: Fill the stats the set lacks; don't stack accuracy/focus past the requirement
gearRecs.why: Balanced stats show more power: duplicates add little, missing stats a lot. An accuracy/focus-heavy set lowers power and can drop the bracket.

gearRecs.substats: Accuracy 900–1,000+, focus for debuffers
gearRecs.why: 900 accuracy is enough to 328 post-easing; ND러너 keeps about 1,000 past 300, calls 1,300 wasted. Take accuracy pieces that also add power.

gearRecs.substats: Skill AMP + crit rate (accuracy or focus if short)
gearRecs.why: Skill AMP is the must-have weapon line, then crit; stage enemies lack crit resistance, so one guide prefers crit rate. Accuracy or focus if short.

gearRecs.substats: Crit resist: power padding only
gearRecs.why: Useless in the fight (stage mobs don't crit) but inflates displayed power; keep it only when the bracket line is what's missing.

gearRecs.substats: Skill AMP + Skill Haste (accuracy or focus if short)
gearRecs.why: About three Skill Haste lines across accessories keep heals and buffs turning; one 240-30 GingerCraven clear needed 20+ from gear.

gearRecs.substats: Anything with the highest power (DR + HP when survival fails)
gearRecs.why: Armour is taken for power. When the front line dies (GingerCraven's burst before the easing), damage reduction and HP replace crit resist and evasion.

gearRecs.substats: A pure-power preset for the bracket line, a Skill Haste preset for auto
gearRecs.why: Two presets: all Skill Haste for auto, pure power when sitting just under a bracket line. The 301-27 15% clear used one named 뻥투.

gearRecs.substats: Arena-style preset: Skill Haste first, then Skill AMP, crit rate, crit damage, damage reduction; no accuracy or focus
gearRecs.why: Damage and cast rate: the boss isn't accuracy-gated like stages. Most top posts reuse their arena preset.

gearRecs.substats: One move-speed line
gearRecs.why: Milk arrives sooner: one poster went 50-60G to 75.4G on lower displayed power; others see Milk come out at once.

gearRecs.substats: Flat-ATK (깡공) Conquest preset
gearRecs.why: The 428.96G run used it; one poster felt 10–15% more after a flat-ATK weapon swap.

gearRecs.substats: The Guild Conquest preset
gearRecs.why: One account gained 100G on it vs 30G on arena, one run each; 서신우 saw no misses; 섬영's weekly best used it.

gearRecs.substats: Higher displayed power
gearRecs.why: 뱅국 picks gear for power; other guides trade it for damage lines, and the move-speed case scored higher on less power.

mechanics.title: Pomegranate's beams (빨대)
mechanics.body: +69% skill amp for 9 s to the highest-ATK allies (ATK, not power), never herself. Her level and ATK don't change it.

mechanics.title: Beam count: 3 + 다발
mechanics.body: 3 beams with no 다발, 5 with 다발 2 (Cheesecake, Herb, or Chardonnay from 10-08), 6 with 다발 3 (Tiger Lily). Levels don't stack: the highest held counts, so nobody reports more than 6.

mechanics.title: Who grants 다발 (Volley)
mechanics.body: Cheesecake's orbiting letters, Herb's heal, Tiger Lily's mount and, from 10-08, Chardonnay's line barrier, per the skill texts. Tiger Lily's reaches only allies near her.

mechanics.title: The 다발 retry checklist
mechanics.body: Pomegranate on 다발 2 by 45 s left and 다발 3 by 27 s left. Miss 다발 3 and the run stays on 5 beams.

mechanics.title: Milk and the welfare perks
mechanics.body: Milk must be ATK #1: 열정페이 (+20% ATK, −20% max HP) and 초고속승진 (+7% ATK) go to the highest-ATK ally. The HP cut kills her by 17 s.

mechanics.title: Cheesecake's buff overrides Milk's
mechanics.body: A cookie holding both keeps only Cheesecake's: 228K ATK vs 483K with Milk's alone. Best case: Cheesecake buffs Milk (667K).

mechanics.title: Crit above 100%
mechanics.body: Past 100% effective crit rate, +10% crit dmg beats +10% crit rate. The raid boss has no crit resistance.

mechanics.title: Crit tiers
mechanics.body: Crit rate past 100% rolls extra tiers: 200% always crits twice; 198% crits once plus 98% for a second. Each tier adds 50% + bonus crit dmg.

mechanics.title: Skill haste formula
mechanics.body: Cooldown = base × 100 / (100 + haste): 50 haste cuts 33%, not 50%. Only the parent skill's cooldown is hasted. No cap found.

mechanics.title: Brightseeker haste breakpoint
mechanics.body: Haste pays steeply to about 40, then stalls (model of a 43 s fight). Past about 58, her drones split onto adds.

mechanics.title: Haste when the team dies at the slam
mechanics.body: In a 30 s fight, skill amp beats haste: going from 20 to 40 haste loses about 3.4%.

mechanics.title: Lift resistance
mechanics.body: Airborne 0.4 s or more cancels a skill. Resistance: 20% base, 48% with Pinot, 64% with Pinot plus a 20% pet.

mechanics.title: Lift resistance stacking
mechanics.body: Stacks as base + extra − base×extra. Candy Shade Pouch gives up to 30% (plus 12.5% HP).

mechanics.title: Skill amp nerf (8/27)
mechanics.body: Skill amp no longer boosts stat-reduction debuffs (Dark Choco's too) or damage-reduction buffs; enemy DEF floors at 0. So Dark Choco runs haste.

mechanics.title: Boss
mechanics.body: 지나치게 무거워진 피냐타 is Dark, weak to Light (Brightseeker). Slam at 30 s elapsed; super-jump wipe at 17 s left. Accuracy, focus, crit resistance: useless here.

mechanics.title: Octo Wasabi pet
mechanics.body: +40% duration-synergy effect. +10% ATK to duration-synergy allies per the card; posters and a video guide measure +8% on Scorpion's entry (disputed).

mechanics.title: Octo Wasabi's hidden ATK
mechanics.body: The bonus isn't on the stat screen: add it by hand when tuning ATK order. It can reshuffle the order mid-fight.

mechanics.title: Tea Knight is raid-only
mechanics.body: Every 10 s: a 155.2% ATK strike and all allies +70% Boss DMG for 10 s (+45% at lowest grade). Guild Conquest only.

mechanics.title: Tea Knight causes most stray beams
mechanics.body: She stands at the front and often misses Milk's buff, so a beam jumps elsewhere.

mechanics.title: Surviving the 17 s wipe
mechanics.body: First-round floor, stated: about 9M HP with 45% DR per survivor; a 9.4M HP, 45.6% DR Brightseeker lived to ~9 s left. Season 6 posts say 10–13M+ at 39–43% DR.

mechanics.title: Who still dies at the wipe
mechanics.body: The ATK-order carries (about 5M HP) and Milk (열정페이's HP cut).

mechanics.title: Survival and the Season 5 jump
mechanics.body: Every ≥2T screen that shows the timer or a survival note outlives the wipe; 캔디애플's Melon Soda team doesn't. Earlier, at 21G account power, four carries hit to 8 s left.

mechanics.title: No manual control since 9/10
mechanics.body: Removed on 9/10: placement comes from composition alone. So a Lv.1 Cherry is carried to push Brightseeker in front of Macaron.

mechanics.title: Skill amp scales Milk's buff (8/13)
mechanics.body: Since 8/13, skill amp scales Milk's ATK buff: why Milk is ATK #1 and leader in every top deck.

mechanics.title: Weapon: crit rate or crit dmg
mechanics.body: At equal skill amp, read crit rate after Macaron's buff: last two digits under 30, take crit dmg; 30+, crit rate. More skill amp beats both.

mechanics.title: HP to survive the slam
mechanics.body: About 3.5–4M HP survives the 30 s slam. Level barely matters: gear and lab HP research give even a Lv.1 cookie about 4M.

mechanics.title: Sugar rune slots and rolls
mechanics.body: Slots unlock at ★6, two at ★8, two at ★10. Line maxima: ATK% 7, crit rate 8, crit dmg 8, skill amp 5 (SSR), haste +5 (SSR; SR +3).

mechanics.title: Gear enhancement
mechanics.body: Sub-options jump at +5, +10, +15 and +20 (+130% at +15, +200% at +20). Only accessory groups roll haste: max +4.6 at +15.

mechanics.title: Piñata's element
mechanics.body: Dark: the boss's lobby screen shows the moon icon.

mechanics.title: Piñata's weakness
mechanics.body: Light: the boss's lobby screen marks the sun icon as its weakness (약점).

mechanics.title: How a Piñata run is scored
mechanics.body: Damage dealt before the 60 s timer ends. A wipe keeps what it dealt: one full wipe at the 30 s slam still scored over 100배.

mechanics.title: Buffs scale with the caster's skill amp
mechanics.body: buff = floor(base × value × (1 + skill amp ÷ 100)), with the caster's skill amp, not the receiver's. From Sugar Pocket's calculator code, not the client.

mechanics.title: A share-of-stat buff scales with that stat
mechanics.body: When a buff's value is a share of the caster's ATK or HP, that stat is the base, so it scales the buff too.

mechanics.title: Debuff application chance
mechanics.body: Chance = base × (caster focus ÷ target resist + focus% − resist%), clamped 0–100%; no resist counts as 1. No skill amp. Calculator code, not the client.

mechanics.title: Piñata's English name
mechanics.body: Extra-Stuffed Piñata, per the official English 8/27 notes and crumb.gg. One guide says Overly Heavy Pinata; the English client's data is unchecked.

mechanics.title: Why fillers sit at Lv.1
mechanics.body: Beams go to the highest-ATK allies (ATK, not power), so cookies that shouldn't take one stay low, under the recipients in ATK.

mechanics.title: Scorpion, the tuned exception
mechanics.body: Levelled to sit exactly 7th in ATK, so a stray beam lands on her, not on a filler.

mechanics.title: Fillers levelled for survival
mechanics.body: Once carries outlive the wipe, raising fillers to just under the beam line lets them survive too and add chip damage: 2T 204G.

mechanics.title: Damage reduction ramps every 12 s
mechanics.body: The boss takes full damage to 10 s elapsed, then 10/30/50/70/90% less from 10/22/34/46/58 s, ≈10.5 s after each 12 s spawner. Early damage counts most.

mechanics.title: Only the boss's damage scores
mechanics.body: Hits on summons don't count. Two things multiply into the wipe: summon ATK (1.7K → 250M) and the boss's ATK, ×25,001 in its 42.5 s wave on every ally.

mechanics.title: What outliving the wipe is worth
mechanics.body: Disputed: posters put it at +300–600G for a run that reaches 1.5T by 17 s; a guide says keep damage pets and take the wipe.

mechanics.title: HP that outlives the wipe
mechanics.body: Season 7, Lv.114–118: about 9M+ in-game survives, stated. Season 6, Lv.100: posters said 10–13M+; a 13.4M HP, 43% DR Brightseeker lived to ~7 s left, a 10.4M HP, 39% DR Milk died, and 5–9M only reached 17 s.

mechanics.title: Pet for the wipe
mechanics.body: Panda Dumpling places Tiger Lily better while the team dies at 17 s (5–9M HP); Candy Shade Pouch's HP wins once carries survive.

mechanics.title: Stat weights on the Season 6 #1's account
mechanics.body: Leaked, second-hand: skill amp +1% ≈ +2% damage; crit rate +15% ≈ +3%; crit dmg +15% ≈ +4%; ATK +650 ≈ +2.5%. His own calculator's sample shows far less: skill amp +1% ≈ +0.45%, crit dmg +1% ≈ +0.38%.

mechanics.title: Chardonnay grants 다발 1–2, not 3 (from 10-08)
mechanics.body: As released: her 1x8 line barrier gives 다발 1–2, CRIT% +60–120% and Push RES 40–60% for 5 s, every 4 s, scaling with stars.

mechanics.title: Tiger Lily's 다발 3 vs Chardonnay's Push RES
mechanics.body: Disputed: Push RES keeps Pomegranate from being pushed into Tiger Lily's range, so 다발 3 lands only sometimes. One poster tunes speed for 2 of 3 runs.

mechanics.title: 탄속 holders take beams first
mechanics.body: Milk and Chardonnay, who receive 탄속, take Pomegranate's beams at any ATK, even ATK 1. The remaining beams go by ATK.

mechanics.title: Six recipients, six beams
mechanics.body: Milk, Chardonnay, Brightseeker, Skating Queen, Tea Knight and Cheesecake all need a beam; 다발 2 gives 5, so Tiger Lily stays for the sixth.

mechanics.title: Crit buffs don't stack
mechanics.body: Macaron's and Chardonnay's crit buffs don't stack, so Chardonnay replaces Macaron. Her line reaches far wider than Macaron's.

mechanics.title: Chardonnay's crit buff scales with skill amp
mechanics.body: Her skill text marks only Push RES as unaffected by skill amp, so her crit buff grows with it.

mechanics.title: Level 120 needs account level 200
mechanics.body: Cookie Lv.120 unlocks at Crumble level 200; on 10-08 and 10-09 maxed cores show Lv.115–118. 100 → 120 costs about 252M EXP per cookie.

mechanics.title: Season 7: the wipe is survivable at Lv.118
mechanics.body: With Lv.114–118 cores, every cookie outlives 17 s in 서신우's 2.5T run; Lv.1 fillers at 9.2M in-game HP (stated) are alive at 13.7 s left, and fillers at Lv.50–90 live to 5.8 s.

mechanics.title: Season 7 keeps the Piñata
mechanics.body: Season 7 (10-08 16:00 to 10-12 12:00 KST) runs on the same Extra-Stuffed Piñata: Dark, weak to Light, phase table unchanged.

mechanics.title: Format
mechanics.body: Auto-battle: your attack team against another player's saved defense. No bans, picks or rounds.

mechanics.title: Teams
mechanics.body: Attack and defense are set separately. Refreshing the opponent list can cost crystals.

mechanics.title: Auto-repeat
mechanics.body: Continuous challenge (auto-repeat attacks) since 2026-09-10.

mechanics.title: Team size
mechanics.body: 12 cookies, 3 pets, a captain and two merc perks per side.

mechanics.title: Battle length
mechanics.body: About 60 s. Near the end '종료 임박' appears and damage rises.

mechanics.title: Matchmaking
mechanics.body: Per server. Opponent names and power are visible; their gear isn't.

mechanics.title: Tickets
mechanics.body: One Arena ticket every 2 h; a free opponent refresh every 30 min.

mechanics.title: Seasons
mechanics.body: About two weeks each, closing 12:00 KST. Season 5 still live on 10-06.

mechanics.title: Tiers
mechanics.body: Champion 1–3 go to ranks 1–3. Master 4 to Grand Master 1 promote by absolute rank.

mechanics.title: Points
mechanics.body: An attack win pays +15 to +25. A failed defense costs 1–5.

mechanics.title: Revenge
mechanics.body: Revenge attacks from the defense log recoup more than the loss.

mechanics.title: Rewards
mechanics.body: Wins pay Fame (Boss, Element, Crit DMG levels) and Victory Medals.

mechanics.title: Promotion rewards
mechanics.body: First promotions pay diamonds: 4,000 for Elite Master 1 and Grand Master 3, 6,000 for Grand Master 2.

mechanics.title: Stats that count
mechanics.body: Level, promotion, codex, gear, plate, sugar runes and pet ownership effects (in-game help).

mechanics.title: Stats that don't
mechanics.body: Breakthrough, Stellar Link and the labs don't count, so displayed power overstates PvP strength.

mechanics.title: Merc perks
mechanics.body: Disputed: the in-game help omits them. The 10-08 patch adds help text on how they apply.

mechanics.title: Level cap
mechanics.body: Level counts, so the 10-08 cap raise to Lv.120 lifts Arena power.

mechanics.title: Power bracket
mechanics.body: The PvE power bracket is fixed at 100% in PvP.

mechanics.title: Season buffs
mechanics.body: No season passive in regular Arena. Season 1 skipped the defense's DR; fixed from Season 2.

mechanics.title: Format
mechanics.body: The same auto-battle as Arena, run beside it, in one cross-server pool.

mechanics.title: Presets
mechanics.body: Its own 5 presets for attack and defense. Levels can't be changed there.

mechanics.title: Team size
mechanics.body: Up to 12 cookies and 3 pets. Empty slots are legal.

mechanics.title: Battle length
mechanics.body: About 60 s with a visible countdown.

mechanics.title: Season 1
mechanics.body: 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-08, battles closing 12:00 KST.

mechanics.title: Season 2
mechanics.body: Opens with the 10-08 update. Client data: 10-08 14:00 to 10-21 12:00 KST.

mechanics.title: Season 1 buff
mechanics.body: Charge cookies +30% max HP; all cookies and summons +30% DR. Both teams.

mechanics.title: Season buffs rotate
mechanics.body: Each season has its own passive. Season 2's was unannounced on 10-07.

mechanics.title: Tickets
mechanics.body: 5 free a day, refilled at 00:00; extras cost 1,000 mileage each.

mechanics.title: Points
mechanics.body: The win value shows before the fight. A held defense gives +1 or +2; a lost one −1 to −5.

mechanics.title: Promotion gems
mechanics.body: First promotions pay gems: out of Diamond 2 1,200, out of Master 2 1,800, into Elite Master 5 2,000, into Grand Master 3 4,000.

mechanics.title: Medals
mechanics.body: +175 medals per win or held defense at Master and Elite Master, up from +125.

mechanics.title: Anonymous opponents
mechanics.body: Above 2,000 points opponents show as 익명의 도전자, with power and levels as ???.

mechanics.title: Hidden defenders
mechanics.body: Above 2,000 points 2–3 of the 12 defenders show as hidden placeholders on attack screens. Defense logs show all 12.

mechanics.title: Revenge
mechanics.body: Revenge screens show 25–39 points; one player says a revenge paid only +3.

mechanics.title: Shop reset
mechanics.body: Disputed: posters say the Rumble shop resets every two weeks, monthly, or not at all.

mechanics.title: Leagues
mechanics.body: Platinum, Diamond, Master 5–1, Elite Master 5–1, Grand Master 3–1, Champion 3–1.

mechanics.title: Top leagues
mechanics.body: Grand Master 3/2/1 need 3,000 points and top 100/30/10; Champion 3/2/1 need 3,200 and top 3/2/1.

mechanics.title: Reward cliff
mechanics.body: Ranks ~101 to ~2,300 sat in Elite Master 1 on 10-07, all on the same reward.

mechanics.title: Daily rewards
mechanics.body: Daily mail: 2,500 medals to the top 100, 2,000 to Master top 5–30%.

mechanics.title: Shop
mechanics.body: Medals buy dungeon keys, chocolate, syrup, Stella rune rewards and a random box.

mechanics.title: Stats that count
mechanics.body: Players say stars and gear count, breakthrough and labs don't. No official text.

mechanics.title: Ruling: Bari's star threshold against Rye
mechanics.body: Rye usually holds Bari to about 6★; from 7–8★ built Bari usually wins at equal spec. Wins against 8–10★ Bari are reported.

mechanics.title: Ruling: 5★ Bari is a floor
mechanics.body: Under 5★ Soul Guidance covers one charger and the Bari deck loses to Rye.

mechanics.title: Ruling: 'Rye beats Bari' is mostly Rumble
mechanics.body: Rumble's +30% DR keeps Rye's tanks alive; in regular Arena the same deck dies in seconds.

mechanics.title: A set Bari deck
mechanics.body: 'Set' means about 230% unbuffed crit, so the dive crits through Moon Rabbit.

mechanics.title: Attacker advantage
mechanics.body: Many players report defenses losing to equal attackers. Cause untested.

mechanics.title: Attacker advantage: theories
mechanics.body: Perks not applied on defense, or layouts differ between attack and defense. Neither is tested.

mechanics.title: Chargers dive the highest-ATK enemy
mechanics.body: Oven, Cherry Cola and Bari dash at the top-ATK enemy, almost always Milk.

mechanics.title: Lose Milk or Bari, lose the fight
mechanics.body: Passion Pay cuts Milk's HP by 20%, which is why divers target her.

mechanics.title: Princess Bari's Soul Guidance
mechanics.body: Herself plus one charger (two from 5★): DR, lift and push immunity, aura damage.

mechanics.title: Soul Guidance numbers
mechanics.body: At 8★: 5.5 s cooldown, 32% DR, aura 127.8% of the guided cookie's ATK.

mechanics.title: Moon Rabbit's debuff
mechanics.body: Cuts ATK and crit rate of enemies near her (about −50% / −130% at 9★, datamine).

mechanics.title: Moon Rabbit misses Rye
mechanics.body: Back-line Rye isn't hit by Moon Rabbit's debuff.

mechanics.title: The first cast wins
mechanics.body: Whoever casts first nearly always wins; CC on a cooldown delays the cast.

mechanics.title: Skill Haste has diminishing returns
mechanics.body: Cooldown = base × 100 ÷ (100 + haste).

mechanics.title: DR stacks multiplicatively
mechanics.body: 10% from Icy Birdie and 10% from a perk give 19%, not 20%.

mechanics.title: ATK order routes the buffs
mechanics.body: Pomegranate's beam and Macaron's buff go by ATK rank: Milk first, then the carry.

mechanics.title: ATK order counts every bonus
mechanics.body: Pet, perk and captain ATK% change the order; check it in battle.

mechanics.title: Synergy givers buff receivers first
mechanics.body: Macaron's buff can go to Milky Way instead of along her line.

mechanics.title: Rye in battle
mechanics.body: Buffed Rye went from 17.9K to 146K ATK and from 90% to 221% crit.

mechanics.title: Auto placement goes by range
mechanics.body: Auto-formation places cookies by attack range; equal ranges go left first.

mechanics.title: Formation geometry
mechanics.body: Left to right is back line to front: Macaron (range 7) left, Moon Rabbit (1) right.

mechanics.title: Opponent cards look mirrored
mechanics.body: Read slots only from your own formation screen.

mechanics.title: Stars on cards
mechanics.body: Yellow stars count to 5; each pink star above that adds one.

mechanics.title: Decoys and targeting
mechanics.body: Rye's first volley fires where she faces; an isolated decoy can soak it.

mechanics.title: Evasion against accuracy
mechanics.body: About 1,200 evasion beats arena presets; one accuracy line breaks it.

mechanics.title: Merc Lv.4 perks decide mirrors
mechanics.body: Lv.4 unlocks a second perk; in the Rye mirror the side without perks loses.

mechanics.title: Healing reduction ended the heal meta
mechanics.body: Pinot's heal cut beats heal stacks; shields from Ion and Rockstar aren't cut.

mechanics.title: Partly hidden Arena defenses
mechanics.body: A #1's defense showed 8 of 12 cookies; hidden slots also show on ranking cards.

mechanics.title: Displayed power overstates PvP strength
mechanics.body: Power counts stats PvP ignores; 2× power gaps fall routinely.

mechanics.title: Chardonnay (from 10-08)
mechanics.body: SSR Grass support: a wall raising crit and push RES along a line, plus Volley.

mechanics.title: Chardonnay numbers (datamine)
mechanics.body: Crit +50→100%, Volley +100→200%, push RES +40→60%, for 5 s every 4 s.

mechanics.title: Ruling: one 12-cookie team, not 'turtle vs charge'
mechanics.body: 8-cookie boards are the standard 12 with hidden slots.

mechanics.title: Ruling: where 'Rye beats Bari' holds
mechanics.body: Mid-ladder, at similar or lower power. Not against finished Bari at the top.

mechanics.title: What the Season 1 buff does
mechanics.body: +30% Charge HP made Oven meta; +30% DR lets Rye decks survive the dive.

mechanics.title: Season 2 may end the charge core
mechanics.body: Players expect Bari and Oven to fall if the Charge buff rotates out.

mechanics.title: Princess Bari's Soul Guidance
mechanics.body: Stacks with the Charge HP buff, which is why a 1★ Bari still tops damage.

mechanics.title: Bari's stars in Rumble
mechanics.body: Bari decks win at 2–3★ here; posters disagree whether 5★ or 8★ is the floor.

mechanics.title: ATK order routes the buffs
mechanics.body: Rye decks set Milk › Rye ≥ Pomegranate with ATK% on Rye.

mechanics.title: Decoy Oven
mechanics.body: Enemy chargers chase your top-ATK cookie; an Oven out-ATKing Milk pulls them together.

mechanics.title: Moon Rabbit and Ion hold the dive
mechanics.body: Moon Rabbit's ATK-down plus Ion's shields form the wall charge decks can't break.

mechanics.title: Chargers with haste run in alone
mechanics.body: Hasted chargers engage before Milk's and Pomegranate's buffs land.

mechanics.title: crumb.gg grids sort by range
mechanics.body: Board grids list cookies by attack range, not position: membership, not slots.

mechanics.title: Formation geometry
mechanics.body: Own attack panels show the standard 12 in the same layout as Arena's Bari deck.

mechanics.title: Power doesn't decide rank
mechanics.body: The top account by power (50.8e9) sits 18th on 10-07; #1 has 43.6e9.

mechanics.title: Matchmaking follows your points
mechanics.body: Opponents come from near your points; some leave a 1-cookie defense to drop.

mechanics.title: Evasion is a wildcard
mechanics.body: 1,100–1,500 evasion defenses beat stronger teams until an accuracy line shows up.

mechanics.title: Ladder end is a ticket race
mechanics.body: The top ranks are decided by mileage spent on extra tickets.

mechanics.title: Structure
mechanics.body: Chapters of 30 stages (243-30). The -10, -20 and -30 stages hold the bosses (or packs of up to ten); the rest are mob stages.

mechanics.title: The end and the Rift
mechanics.body: Stages run to 328-30 since 2026-09-10; clearing 328-30 opens the Dimensional Rift.

mechanics.title: Team and presets
mechanics.body: 12 cookies, 3 pets, a captain and mercenary band perks, as in the other modes.

mechanics.title: Which gear preset fights
mechanics.body: The stage uses the preset chosen on the formation (편성) screen, not the gear menu's; presets switch between stage, arena and conquest sets.

mechanics.title: Idle rewards and boss retries
mechanics.body: Your parked stage sets idle rewards. Bosses start from a boss summon; with auto-summon on, a deck retries unattended.

mechanics.title: The power gate is a step function on final damage
mechanics.body: Team power ÷ the stage's recommended power picks a bracket; the bracket multiplies final damage, last in crumblehub's formula (after defence, element, boss damage, crit).

mechanics.title: No interpolation between steps
mechanics.body: 39.9% of recommended power fights at 15%, 40.0% at 35%. '35% 단' means pushing at 40–59% of recommended power; '15%' at 20–39%.

mechanics.title: What the gate does not touch
mechanics.body: Only your team's damage is cut: boss damage is unchanged, and your stats keep counting past the 120% cap. PvP's correction is fixed at 100%.

mechanics.title: The same table gates other content
mechanics.body: The bracket table also gates the daily dungeons, the Implant Tower and the Dimensional Rift.

mechanics.title: Team power is the formation's displayed power, and it can be padded
mechanics.body: The gate reads formation-screen power: gear, sugar runes, plates, guild and pets. Leaving a guild dropped one player from 35% to 15%.

mechanics.title: How pushers pad power
mechanics.body: Gear rolled 'purely for power' (뻥투), crit-resist lines (a cape: 3.99M with one, 2.82M without) and SSR rune lines kept until the Rift (+3–4M each).

mechanics.title: Just short is a full bracket down
mechanics.body: 0.6M short of the 40% line (971.8M against 972.5M at 271-11) fought at 15%.

mechanics.title: Accuracy and focus are a second gate per stage
mechanics.body: Each stage has an accuracy requirement (enemy evasion) and a focus one (enemy resistance). At it, attacks hit 100% and debuffs land as listed; below, they miss.

mechanics.title: Accuracy caps, focus keeps climbing
mechanics.body: Game data 1.4.002: accuracy stops rising at 1,203.5 from about chapter 248 to 328-30; focus keeps rising to 1,161.5 at 328-30.

mechanics.title: What missing accuracy costs
mechanics.body: About 10% more misses per 100 accuracy short, per one poster; 950 accuracy hit about 79% at 270-18 before the easing.

mechanics.title: How much accuracy the pushers actually run
mechanics.body: Post-easing, 900 accuracy is called enough to 328; ND러너 runs 900–1,000 on stages and 1,000+ past 300. 1,300 is wasted.

mechanics.title: Before the easing, accuracy was tight
mechanics.body: 35% pushers wanted 1,000–1,100+ accuracy; dropping from 1,150 to 930 broke clears around chapter 250.

mechanics.title: Focus is for debuffers; 15% and the Rift need more
mechanics.body: Focus matters for Dark Choco and Scorpion's shred ('drop Dark Choco's focus and it's an empty can'). At 15% and in the Rift every miss costs more.

mechanics.title: The 2026-09-23 easing lowered recommended power and enemy stats
mechanics.body: Update 1.4.002 cut recommended power, enemy ATK and HP from almost nothing at 169-1 to about 30% at 248-30 (2.00G → 1.40G) and 36% at 328-30 (15.61G → 10.00G).

mechanics.title: Accuracy requirements didn't change
mechanics.body: 248-30 stayed at 1,203 accuracy. One player's 55% reach still moved from chapter 257 to 273 overnight.

mechanics.title: Bosses rebalanced (169-1 to 248-30)
mechanics.body: Cool Mint, Rowdy Biker, Rowdy Truck, GingerCraven, Cream Eagle, Tainted Ent, Redberry Assassin, Choco Werehound Princess.

mechanics.title: Chapters cycle through eight zones with fixed boss slots
mechanics.body: Chapter c is zone ((c − 1) mod 8) + 1: grassland, beach, ruined city, desert, mushroom zone, plaza, lava zone, snowfield. Layouts repeat from chapter 169.

mechanics.title: The -30 boss per zone
mechanics.body: Cool Mint: grassland, beach, plaza. GingerCraven (비겁한 쿠키): ruined city, snowfield. Ginkgoblin Stormer: desert. Tainted Ent: mushroom zone. Magma Sugar Waffle Lizard: lava zone.

mechanics.title: The -10 and -20 bosses
mechanics.body: Ruined city: three Rowdy Bikers (-10), the Rowdy Truck (-20). Plaza: ten Redberry Assassins (-10), Choco Werehound Princess (망치공주, -20). The rest are mob stages, several with ten enemies.

mechanics.title: GingerCraven (비겁이) is the wall at every bracket
mechanics.body: The ruined-city and snowfield -30 boss flees, fears the team and outlasts low damage: where a bracket stops working ('비겁이 컷').

mechanics.title: Before the easing: 35% at best
mechanics.body: GingerCraven needed 35% at best; many pushers took it at 55% with padded power.

mechanics.title: At 15%, GingerCraven fails
mechanics.body: 256-30 at 980M left it at 41% after an hour; another pusher removed about 20% of its HP at 15%, then cleared first try at 35%.

mechanics.title: Bring a dedicated GingerCraven deck
mechanics.body: Scorpion, Lime or Tiger Lily, Ion, and damage-reduction perks and pets.

mechanics.title: When 35% keeps failing, climb to 55%
mechanics.body: Swap filler support for power (GingerBright → Pinot Noir, Grapevine → Brightseeker) to reach 55%; clear within about 20 tries, not hours at 35%.

mechanics.title: Launch bosses: bring Panda Dumpling
mechanics.body: Panda Dumpling (판다만두) as third pet, even at low level, for Lift RES and HP. Launchers: Cool Mint, Werehound Princess, Tainted Ent, King Choco Drop.

mechanics.title: Redberry Assassin and the truck need hands
mechanics.body: Redberry packs wipe and scatter: swap two melee for Jungle Warrior or Tiger Lily and Rye and lure them to the 6 o'clock stairs, or go area rapid-fire.

mechanics.title: Rowdy Truck: kite, then auto
mechanics.body: Kite it in circles at 7 or 9 o'clock until the team's first heal (about 26 s in), then leave it to auto.

mechanics.title: Where 15% works and where it doesn't
mechanics.body: 15% clears are mob stages and weak bosses: 289-30 Cool Mint at 1.29G (screenshot); 271-11 (Lava Waffle Lizard pack) at 971.8M; 301-27 and 301-28 at 2.05G by hand.

mechanics.title: Walls at 15%
mechanics.body: The -30 bosses but Cool Mint, the bikers, truck, eagle and Redberry packs are walls at 15%; GingerCraven at 15% is 'nearly impossible'.

mechanics.title: An unshown 15% claim
mechanics.body: 328-30 at 'just over 3G' with Bari 9★ and Cherry Cola 10★: claimed, no screenshot.

mechanics.title: After the easing, 35% pushes to 328-30
mechanics.body: Since 2026-09-23, 35% clears to the end: 328-30 GingerCraven at 4.00G, 4.06G and 4.2G; 312-30 at 2.74G; 266-30 Cool Mint on auto at 1.17G.

mechanics.title: Runs now fail on damage, not survival
mechanics.body: The 35% line at 328-30 is 4.00G (40% of 10.00G). Tanks and Herb leave the deck for damage and Rockstar.

mechanics.title: Push, then park at the highest clear
mechanics.body: Idle rewards follow the stage you park on: push until stuck, park on the highest clear, reinvest, push again.

mechanics.title: 55% by hand, stop at 35%
mechanics.body: Guides call about 55% of recommended a realistic manual target and about 35% the point to stop and farm; tryhards push at 35%, mob stages at 15%.

mechanics.title: Boss auto-summon retries unattended
mechanics.body: With 자동 소환 예약 on, a deck retries a boss on auto indefinitely; one 264-30 clear came after 30 minutes by hand, then unattended retries.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: rules
mechanics.body: Opens at 328-30. Seasonal (season 1: 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-08, levels 1–100; later seasons 101–200) and boss-only: one boss fight per level.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: recommended power
mechanics.body: From 10.00G at level 1 to about 1,800G at level 100.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: 차원의 힘 (Dimensional Energy)
mechanics.body: A Rift-only stat that fills per minute in the Rift and raises ATK, DEF and HP amplification, crit, accuracy and focus there only.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: 차원의 힘 inflates power
mechanics.body: Displayed power grows with it: 4.0G to 8.05G by 차원의 힘 Lv.4; ND러너 showed 22G against about 5G real.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: rewards
mechanics.body: Per-level clears (a profile frame at 10; ND러너 names pets at 1 and 20), a 차원의 조각 shop (about 3 a minute), daily and season all-server rankings.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: the power gate applies
mechanics.body: Brackets apply against the level's recommended power and the Rift-inflated team power. One poster felt no penalty; four others and the top player say it applies.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: every level opens with 차원의 힘
mechanics.body: ND러너: 'treat every Rift level as a 35% fight'; each level becomes clearable once enough 차원의 힘 has stacked.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: 15% with full shred, except GingerCraven
mechanics.body: With maximum DEF shred the other bosses fall at 15%; GingerCraven needs 35%.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: bosses and tech
mechanics.body: Boss types repeat: level 3 Werehound Princess, 4 Rowdy Truck, 5 and 15 GingerCraven, 6 Cake Hound Pack, 9 three trucks, 100 GingerCraven. Adds come from both sides.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: top-guild tech
mechanics.body: Stack Scorpion's poison to 20 and DEF shred to 10; add Dark Choco and Devil against the truck; pull the boss to 7 or 9 o'clock.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: five tries, then park
mechanics.body: Give a level about five tries: if 20–30% of its HP comes off, keep trying; else park and level 차원의 힘.

mechanics.title: Dimensional Rift: buffs and pets
mechanics.body: The entrance grants a Charge buff; Octo Wasabi (와사비 문어) is the favoured pet; the Rift-only SSR pet 무한바퀴 raises boss damage there.

mechanics.title: Every Rift boss but GingerCraven goes at 15%, to about level 18
mechanics.body: 15% screenshot clears for every boss but GingerCraven to about level 18; stalls by 28 (dc:80706). GingerCraven only at 35%.

mechanics.title: Rift gear comparisons show inflated stats
mechanics.body: In the Rift an upgrade arrow can lower real power; compare with no preset applied.

mechanics.title: 차원의 힘 climbs about a level a day
mechanics.body: Lv.9-10 around levels 10-15, 16-17 at level 20, 24 at level 33, 28 at level 38 by 10-07.

mechanics.title: A 1.4 hotfix raised Cool Mint's Rift HP
mechanics.body: Cool Mint's Rift base HP 800 → 900 (+12.5%), in an undated 1.4 hotfix entry.

mechanics.title: Entry and keys
mechanics.body: One Crumble Dungeon Key per run, from the Dungeon menu's Challenge Dungeon (도전 던전) tab. Mileage-shop keys stack above the cap; extras only matter for record attempts.

mechanics.title: Entries a day: three or five
mechanics.body: Three a day per the wiki and the newbie guide; lobbies show a counter out of 5, and a Gnome Lab research adds a daily entry.

mechanics.title: Every cookie enters; the top 40 by power deploy first
mechanics.body: The 40 highest-power cookies deploy at once and earn nearly the whole score, so levels decide who's in. Each death brings in the next by power.

mechanics.title: No formation, pets or manual control
mechanics.body: All owned cookies enter and fight on their own. The in-game first-40 label vanished on 2026-09-23; the rule still holds.

mechanics.title: Scoring and the timer
mechanics.body: Score = damage to the Holy Golden Drop (no HP bar). The run ends when the countdown (up to a minute) hits 0 or every cookie dies.

mechanics.title: Time left and milestones
mechanics.body: Top runs end with 0.000 s to about 6 s left. Score milestones pay from 400,000 points up to 1,000,000,000,000.

mechanics.title: Rankings and resets
mechanics.body: Each server has its own boards. Weekly keeps the week's best run, closes Thursday 00:00 KST; daily ranks only that day's runs, closes at midnight.

mechanics.title: Reward mail and the daily run
mechanics.body: Rewards arrive by mail the next day, 12:00-13:00 KST. The day's first run pays 10,000 XP and 3,000 of a gem currency.

mechanics.title: What the boards pay
mechanics.body: Daily: research stones, one-minute speed-ups, top-10 pet tickets. Weekly: coins, XP, top-10 crystals; top 100 earns the 황금빛 광채 title. Milestones: crystals, cosmetics.

mechanics.title: No power penalty reported
mechanics.body: None reported: no recommended-power gate like the stage's. Score scales with power and levels; score ÷ total power is only a normaliser.

mechanics.title: Level is the only lever on who fights
mechanics.body: Deployment is by combat power, not ATK, and power follows level: raise the 40 you want. Unwanted cookies go to Lv.1 (ND러너) or just under 40th (EOG, VART).

mechanics.title: Exact levels since 9/23
mechanics.body: Since 2026-09-23 a long press on level-up opens fine control; that's how players type in exact levels.

mechanics.title: The Rift buff skews the shown power order
mechanics.body: Displayed power includes the Dimensional Rift buff, so the 40 can deploy out of the order the lineup screen shows. Test with a run.

mechanics.title: Pomegranate's beam picks by synergy, then by ATK
mechanics.body: The beam (석류빔, 빨대) hits Projectile Speed synergy holders first, so Milk always, then by live ATK. Other holders would steal it: level them out.

mechanics.title: Who takes the beam after Milk
mechanics.body: The 578G run beams Brightseeker, then Figure and Scorpion; other top lineups put Scorpion second. ND러너 beamed the buffers, Macaron and Figure.

mechanics.title: Synergy-first is unconfirmed
mechanics.body: EOG calls the synergy-first reading unconfirmed; an English guide restating ND러너's method calls it observed behaviour to verify.

mechanics.title: Milk is the engine: captain, top ATK, centre of the formation
mechanics.body: Captain at top ATK in every documented top run. One tester found Passion Pay ranks ATK without the captain's +10%; repliers agreed, ND러너 reportedly disagrees.

mechanics.title: Milk must reach the centre early
mechanics.body: Its stacking ATK buff has a range: keep the formation packed. Milk arriving at once (about 53 s on the countdown) scores high; trailing in scores low.

mechanics.title: Stacked buffs since 9/10
mechanics.body: Before 2026-09-10 a same-type buff replaced a stacked one: Cheesecake erased Milk's stacks, Lime erased Macaron's. Lineups left both out.

mechanics.title: Cheesecake back in since 9/10
mechanics.body: The stronger stacked value now wins. By 9/21 players rated Cheesecake's buff on Milk a top-two factor; the 325.9G run keeps it sixth in ATK.

mechanics.title: Lower Pomegranate to bring Milk out
mechanics.body: Pomegranate near Lv.60 and fewer supports in the 40 get Milk to the front at once (reports of 10-07). Keep Pomegranate inside the 40.

mechanics.title: Chargers and summoners break the formation
mechanics.body: Chargers run around the boss and Milk follows to heal the lowest-HP ally, so the ranged dealers lose every buff. Summoners spread the formation too.

mechanics.title: Level them out, with exceptions
mechanics.body: Out of the 40: the Exclusions page (Princess Bari since 9/23). Kept: Figure and Vampire, which stay at the boss; Red Pepper and Dark Cherry, which draw Milk forward.

mechanics.title: The Holy Golden Drop's patterns
mechanics.body: Per the wiki: a floor squash that knocks cookies back, lightning strikes, and summoned Golden Soldier Drops.

mechanics.title: Boss timings players report
mechanics.body: A slam at about 20 s left kills weak buffers; a jump scatters cookies; a late sweep wipes the team (15 s left at lower power, 8 s at higher).

mechanics.title: EOG's model: the first 13 s decide a run
mechanics.body: A model, not data: the shockwave throws the team back four times, adds score nothing, and the boss raises its damage reduction three times (stacking to five).

mechanics.title: Conquest-only effects don't apply
mechanics.body: Tea Knight's boss-damage buff works only in Guild Conquest, so it gives nothing here; focus still matters for Devil's and Dark Choco's DEF shred.

mechanics.title: Mercenary perks
mechanics.body: Lv.4: Passion Pay (on Milk) plus Rapid Promotion (most) or Like A Family. Lv.3: Rapid Promotion alone; lower: all-stats. One poster ran ATK 20% with '5사격'.

mechanics.title: Like A Family
mechanics.body: Elemental damage per cookie of the most-fielded element. Best for ND러너 and 누리머; 전치 found Rapid Promotion a little higher by score ÷ power, 30+ runs each, too few runs to be sure.

mechanics.title: No pet selection
mechanics.body: No pet slots. EOG reads pets' passives and Collection bonuses as applying to every cookie anyway; pets' ATK bonuses shift the ATK order.

mechanics.title: KR and global share the servers
mechanics.body: Rankings are per server. One client (1.4.002), one server list: KR boards show English- and Chinese-named rivals, and global EOG reports from 'Server 1'.

mechanics.title: Board size
mechanics.body: Weekly participation runs from a few dozen to about 320 players per server.

mechanics.title: Where team power counts
mechanics.body: Only stages and the Dimensional Rift compare team power with a recommended power (record 003's brackets). In Arena and Guild Conquest it decides nothing.

mechanics.title: Team power versus account total
mechanics.body: Team power (팀투, 덱투, 파티투력) is the lineup's figure the gate uses. Account total (총투) sums every cookie; crumb.gg's board shows it (top 500: 21.8G–50.8G, 2026-10-07).

mechanics.title: Arena excludes some sources
mechanics.body: Arena ignores Resolve, Stellar Link, the Gnome Lab, the guild lab and Fame. It counts level, promotion, pet holding effects, the collection, gear, plating and sugar runes.

mechanics.title: Displayed power weights stats unevenly
mechanics.body: Attackers (magic, ranged, burst) carry high power; healers, tanks and supports low, so lineup swaps move team power without new resources.

mechanics.title: Gear power is dynamic
mechanics.body: A stat below the lineup's target counts heavily, then stops once met (an item fell 69.6M → 65M). Accuracy past ~1,000 adds little; crit resistance pads most.

mechanics.title: How power is computed (claimed, decompiled)
mechanics.body: A cookie's power ≈ √(offense × survival) × role weight; team power sums the cookies. So ATK alone moves power by its square root.

mechanics.title: Flat versus percentage stats
mechanics.body: Late, one gear line beats hundreds of Resolve levels: a +87 ATK bow line gave Milk +6k ATK, +200 Resolve ~1k. Resolve is flat; gear gets % bonuses.

mechanics.title: How Stellar Link scales
mechanics.body: The bonus follows the polygon area through a constellation's points, in order. Points open with total cookie stars; later constellations amplify more at the same area.

mechanics.title: Stellar roll cost
mechanics.body: A roll costs 10 Stellar Points unlocked, 220 with 6 points locked, the most you can lock.

mechanics.title: Plating results and the 1.4.002 change
mechanics.body: Since 2026-09-23: cap 25, a shatter drops 2 levels instead of to 10, and Syrup restores it (20 at 15 to 80 at 24).

mechanics.title: Plating outcomes and Syrup
mechanics.body: Each try: great success (+2), success (+1), maintain, decline (from 10) or shatter (from 15). Syrup blocks declines (1–3 a try) and halves shatters (2).

mechanics.title: Oven level sets gear level
mechanics.body: Gear level runs from oven × 3 − 5 to oven × 3; rarer gear enters the draw as oven level rises (Eternal from 31, 0.002% a draw).

mechanics.title: Level can beat rarity
mechanics.body: A lower-rarity piece of higher level can show more power.

mechanics.title: Level 120 from 2026-10-08
mechanics.body: Cap 100 → 120: +64% base stats at 120 for ~252M EXP per cookie; each level past 100 needs 5 more Crumble levels (200 for 120).

mechanics.title: Chests and dungeons scale with progress
mechanics.body: Coin and EXP auto-hunt chests pay by the current stage, so they are worth more opened later.

mechanics.title: Extra dungeon entries compound
mechanics.body: Daily dungeon keys pay by floor (64 a key low, 4,000–6,000 high), so extra entries (Crumble Pass, the 5.5 membership, key packs) compound.

mechanics.title: Sweet Blessing is a spending track
mechanics.body: Perks, not stats: daily dungeon entries, a Wind Archer copy at level 3. About 10% of spend fills it; level 3 under ~100,000 KRW; 12 levels.

mechanics.title: Every dungeon is open every day
mechanics.body: Each has a fixed boss, element and key; stages rise in recommended power. No weekday rotation.

mechanics.title: Stage cap 770
mechanics.body: Raised from 570 to 770 on 9/23; the 10-08 update didn't raise it.

mechanics.title: Keys and sweeps
mechanics.body: 3 keys a day, up to 6; any cleared stage can be swept; repeat toggle (연속 도전) reruns.

mechanics.title: Below recommended power, damage drops
mechanics.body: The stage power brackets apply: auto decks fail when the damage correction falls to about 35%.

mechanics.title: One boss at every stage: the Dark Librarian
mechanics.body: Every capture from 524 to 746 shows the same Librarian, Dark, weak to Light. No dungeon rotates by weekday.

mechanics.title: Two opening pushes; enter at 47–48 s
mechanics.body: A first slam near 53 s, a double push ending about 48 s. Manual players enter right after it; walking in early gets the team hit again.

mechanics.title: Later hits near 38 s; re-entry about 32 s
mechanics.body: A commenter times another hit at 38 s; one manual guide re-enters at 32 s after pulling out.

mechanics.title: Pushes every few seconds shove the team out of the book ring
mechanics.body: The team heals safely outside the books, then re-enters. Knockback resistance helps: Princess Bari, the Little Ghost pet.

mechanics.title: Flying book rows do the damage
mechanics.body: A book hit leaves Milk standing still. Manual players park in the gap between book rows.

mechanics.title: Milk, Brightseeker or Pomegranate dying loses the run
mechanics.body: Auto works because Milk and the shields absorb the opening; then Brightseeker gets two or more skill casts.

mechanics.title: Low power caps damage
mechanics.body: At a 35% damage correction (power far under recommended) the auto deck stops working.

mechanics.title: Retry is the method
mechanics.body: Every auto source says to keep pressing retry: losses come from the opening, and a rerun with the same deck often clears.

mechanics.title: Disputed: one EXP dealer or more
mechanics.body: The 724 and 746 decks run Brightseeker alone; VART and 누리머 add Rye; one poster argues extra dealers clear better.

mechanics.title: Disputed: does EXP auto hold past 720
mechanics.body: 746 cleared with no input; others stall at 746 with more power, call the deck a one-day fix, or say 720 needs control.

mechanics.title: Disputed: the EXP gear preset
mechanics.body: Conquest (damage-reduction) preset is steadier per several posts; others need the stage preset's damage; some use arena plus Rooty for accuracy.

mechanics.title: Projectile Speed pet tipped the EXP deck
mechanics.body: Furball Pup adds Projectile Speed synergy and ATK; the 746 poster calls it the key.

mechanics.title: Armor Repair in nearly every EXP deck
mechanics.body: Three or more tanks give allies 10% damage reduction; Hound, Ion and Moon Rabbit are there for it.

mechanics.title: Disputed: the second perk
mechanics.body: Health Insurance (+5% max HP with two supports) or Passion Pay (+20% ATK on the top-ATK ally, −20% its HP). 아포 says switch to HP if cookies die entering at 48 s.

mechanics.title: Other dungeons favour damage perks
mechanics.body: Passion Pay with Rapid Promotion or Like A Family; one guide keeps Health Insurance plus Armor Repair for EXP only.

mechanics.title: Scarabs keep their distance
mechanics.body: They back off when approached and close in when the team holds still. Sit in a corner and let them bunch.

mechanics.title: Hold 7 o'clock until about 42 s
mechanics.body: Or release at 50 s. Near the cap the corner stops working; the 770 clears steer from 1 o'clock or circle the corridor.

mechanics.title: Frogs shoot hard; fight from the 5 o'clock corner
mechanics.body: Runs fail when cookies die first. 5 o'clock is now preferred over 7.

mechanics.title: Cream Puff's field launches the frogs
mechanics.body: Frogs bounce in its field. At about 30% skill haste, with Milk and pet duration, the field never drops.

mechanics.title: Jellies spawn under the team and explode
mechanics.body: They keep dropping in until about 40% remain; an explosion can wipe the team. Long fights risk the timer.

mechanics.title: Opening knock-up: cast Pinot Noir first
mechanics.body: The golem's first attack launches the team into the air.

mechanics.title: Green orbs at 53, 45, 37 and 29 s
mechanics.body: Eight seconds apart; manual players dodge them on those beats.

mechanics.title: Keys: 3 a day, up to 6
mechanics.body: Blessing (축복), the permanent ₩5.5k pass and the Crumble Pass add keys; Saturdays and Sundays add more.

mechanics.title: More keys: shops and packs
mechanics.body: The mileage and arena shops sell keys, and a ₩6,000 key pack exists. Bought keys stack above the cap.

mechanics.title: Unknown: does a lost run return its key
mechanics.body: No capture states it. Guides treat losses as free retries, which suggests a key is spent only on a clear.

mechanics.title: Sweep (소탕) once stuck
mechanics.body: Each stage pays a one-time first-clear reward, so players push before sweeping, then sweep at their wall.

rngFactors.effect: Beams follow ATK. A cookie missing Milk's buff (often Tea Knight) shifts the order, and a beam jumps to someone without skill amp.
rngFactors.mitigation: Lv.1 fillers, and Scorpion levelled into 7th in ATK as the catcher. Check in battle: Octo Wasabi adds +8% ATK on entry.

rngFactors.effect: Where cookies stop decides whether Macaron's crit buff reaches Brightseeker and whether Cheesecake's buff overrides Milk's.
rngFactors.mitigation: Cherry forces a straight line; or tune move speed to 0.01 (Melon Soda deck), which still misaligns about 1 run in 4, varying by device.

rngFactors.effect: Records take long sessions: 35 tries for 439G, ~100 runs for 350G, 14 h of macro for 546G. At 1.74G, 1T lands in 1–2 of 10.
rngFactors.mitigation: Budget hours, not minutes. Many top posters run a macro overnight.

rngFactors.effect: Same team, same day: the levelled-filler Cherry account's 100 runs at 2.93G gave 208–783× (mean 477×); 700×+ came once in 20.
rngFactors.mitigation: Score the setup on the median of many runs, not one best; a macro logs no damage, so log by hand first.

rngFactors.effect: Chardonnay's Push RES keeps Pomegranate out of Tiger Lily's range, so the sixth beam lands only in some runs.
rngFactors.mitigation: Retry; or tune move speed on Pinot and Melon Soda (2 of 3 runs, one poster, device-dependent).

rngFactors.effect: With fillers levelled for survival, a cookie within a point of the 6th recipient's ATK steals beams more often.
rngFactors.mitigation: Keep fillers clearly under the 6th recipient after Octo Wasabi's bonus, or retry.

rngFactors.effect: Most teams wipe at 17 s left: 43 s of damage. Surviving adds damage no guide accounts for.
rngFactors.mitigation: Survival is possible: Pomegranate alive at 11.4 s (nv:46283); at 21G total power the carries lived to 8 s left (dc:76583).

rngFactors.factor: Who wins the opening against a dive
rngFactors.effect: The dive kills in about 3.5 s or fails against shields and polymorph.
rngFactors.mitigation: Rockstar in the flex slot, Moon Rabbit as insurance, DR + crit RES below.

rngFactors.effect: Equal defenses lose to attackers far more than they should.
rngFactors.mitigation: Attack late before the 00:00 settlement and farm revenges.

rngFactors.effect: Pet, perk and captain bonuses change live ATK rank, so the beam can miss the carry.
rngFactors.mitigation: Check the order in battle; level supports down to hold it.

rngFactors.effect: An evasion build looks like any other defense.
rngFactors.mitigation: Names are visible: remember evasion defenders and attack them on the stage preset.

rngFactors.effect: Above 2,000 points names, power, levels and 2–3 defender slots are hidden.
rngFactors.mitigation: A visible Macaron, Pinot, Pomegranate and Moon Rabbit almost always means the standard 12.

rngFactors.effect: An evasion defense can beat twice its power; nothing on the card warns you.
rngFactors.mitigation: Two accuracy lines or the stage preset; Mango Toucan gives it away.

rngFactors.effect: At a bracket's bottom, GingerCraven clears hinge on where its fear lands and how long; 35% clears end with 0.6–1.8 s left.
rngFactors.mitigation: Dedicated deck (Scorpion poison to 20, Brightseeker on the boss), DR perks and pets, retries; boss auto-summon retries unattended.

rngFactors.factor: Accuracy and focus below the stage's requirement
rngFactors.effect: Below the accuracy requirement attacks miss (about 10% more per 100 short); below focus, debuffs fail. At 15% and in the Rift, a few misses decide it.
rngFactors.mitigation: Meet the stage's accuracy requirement (1,203.5 caps it from about chapter 248) or at least 900–1,000 after the easing; raise focus for debuffers.

rngFactors.effect: Pomegranate's beam and ATK-targeted perks go to the top-ATK cookies; with the wrong cookie on top, the carry misses them.
rngFactors.mitigation: Check ATK order in battle; steer with rune ATK lines, or lower Skating Queen and Cherry Cola a level or two, Pinot Noir to Lv.75.

rngFactors.effect: On auto, Cherry Cola runs ahead and drags Milk away, so Brightseeker loses Milk's buff; the same deck clears by hand.
rngFactors.mitigation: Drop Cherry Cola from auto decks unless Bari is in, or play the opening by hand.

rngFactors.effect: A Rift level either sheds 20–30% of the boss's HP in a try or doesn't move; the difference is mostly 차원의 힘 level, not luck.
rngFactors.mitigation: Give a level about five tries, then park in the Rift and let 차원의 힘 level up.

rngFactors.effect: Decides the run: early Milk scores high, late Milk low. A support's level or a dealer's runes shift it; a lineup can fail the next day ('세계선').
rngFactors.mitigation: Supports near Lv.70, Pomegranate toward Lv.60, Red Pepper or Dark Cherry in front, a move-speed line; small level changes until Milk comes out.

rngFactors.effect: The same lineup lands tens of G apart: 90-150G on one account, 150-188G for ND러너, 25G against a 45G best at 4.2G.
rngFactors.mitigation: Spend every key (and mileage keys) on record attempts; the weekly board keeps only the best.

rngFactors.factor: Knockback moving buffers out of place
rngFactors.effect: The boss's jump attack can push Figure to one side, where it circles alone outside the buffs.
rngFactors.mitigation: None reported beyond retries.

rngFactors.factor: Power order drifting from what the screen shows
rngFactors.effect: The Rift buff counts in displayed power, so the deployed 40 and their order can differ from the lineup screen, and shift day to day.
rngFactors.mitigation: Check who deploys in a run and adjust; players spend keys to get the order right.
